message:
Manager, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, my tonne count is an enforceable operating limit with a log and fee-funded upkeep, not an illustration.

In plain words one tonne means fifty small boxes filled over four mornings with paper tracking and washing paid by the crate fee. Reusing 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) at 20 kg each, staged as 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250 kg staged intake (E78), moved one 600 by 400 mm crate at a time through the 900 mm door stated in the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) onto two rack rows with 25 mm gaps, with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest produce sold first) tags plus twice-daily thermometer checks and a door log paid by the pay-per-crate model stated in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) with affordability precedent in Preserving Harvests: Fresh Solutions to Food Loss in Kenya (E72). Twenty kilograms is one bag of cement one person can lift and fifty crates in 8.64 cubic metres is a small bedroom holding fourteen adults by weight so everyday scale holds, and a 51st crate is refused at the door because it breaks the energy rule below.

In plain words eight quick daytime openings with the plastic curtain closed is the energy number, a ninth opening breaks cold without breaking any rule unless the tie is written. Reusing 0.169 kWh per day for 8 curtain openings from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) inside 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime with single-crate pass and strip curtain from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight that sets that door term. I declare this the operating limit with attendant crate log, so a ninth opening or propped door is a logged violation that stops further warm intake that day.

In plain words mixed vegetables stay at one safe setting and a warm full load or a dark store is refused, not absorbed, and village repair keeps the fee affordable. Single mixed holding setpoint 5 degrees Celsius stages 250 kg per day with shade plus pre-cool discipline, while full 1000 kg warm at once needing 25.0 kWh from the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) and night loading are refused by rule, and on low charge the Low-Voltage Disconnect (LVD, automatic battery protector that sheds load) sheds new intake until the battery autonomy simulation (E95) recovers, which at 30 percent sun still ends at 3.73 kWh only under staged discipline. From my discipline the BD50F Direct Current Compressor R134a, 12-24V DC & 100-240V AC 50/60Hz source (E102) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer put on the board confirms repairability, because R134a field gauges and spares let a local fridge technician service the store and keep the per-crate fee to washing plus log plus spares instead of specialist call-out.

My position is ready on version two, because tonne plus 8-opening plus refusal now tie to the 0.169 kWh door model and 10.4 kWh load with fee-funded log.
